problem: VLM agents that directly control short waypoint actions are brittle and inefficient over long horizons, while navigation foundation models (NFMs) run bounded episodes without task-level reasoning or memory. Wrapping an NFM as an episodic tool (one instruction in, terminal status and final view out) creates a gap: instruction/intent mismatch, loss of intermediate observations, and no cross-call accumulation.
motivation: Long-horizon physical-world agents need both distant-goal reasoning and reliable closed-loop grounding, and today's VLMs and NFMs each provide only one. EQA is a demanding testbed because evidence may be distant or invisible, so the agent must search several regions and accumulate positive and negative evidence before answering.
key_idea: Couple a VLM reasoning agent with a frozen NFM executor through three evidence-centric channels (intent calls, source-grounded trajectory observations, persistent memory) so isolated navigation rollouts become persistent long-horizon embodied interaction without retraining either model.
insight: The VLM agent and the NFM executor are complementary: with the executor fixed, accuracy rises from 38.2 (no agent) to 74.0 (full agent), and with the agent fixed it rises from 60.9 (random walk) to 74.0 (NFM 8B). The interface matters as much as the models: replacing the three-channel protocol with an episodic interface drops accuracy by far more than any single-channel ablation. Among single components, removing the EQA context state (-4.6) or journey analysis (-4.4) hurts most, so en-route evidence and cross-call state are what matter. (The exact episodic-interface number is a template macro and is not printed.)
method: Intent channel: the agent emits a semantic navigation call (mode, natural-language sub-goal, step budget, constraints) in one of two modes, navigate_to_object or navigate_by_instruction, and the adapter turns it into an NFM episode.

Executor: a frozen 8B Qwen-RobotNav NFM maps four RGB views, pose and an online map to 8 short-horizon waypoints. It runs closed-loop with a 64-step budget per call and an is_stuck recovery flag after 2 consecutive collisions.

Observation channel: keyframes are sampled every 4 steps (max 16) along the rollout, and a VLM summarizer produces a source-grounded journey artifact (sub-goal status, rooms, objects, planning cues, uncertainty), with each mention tied to a keyframe and confidence.

Memory channel: an EQA context state C_t=(history, evidence ledger, unresolved goals), implemented as a write_notebook ledger (max 100 entries). Raw returns are compacted only after being externalized into the ledger.

Answer gating and verification tools: an answer needs visible support, and a negative answer needs coverage of the relevant area. Auxiliary tools include look_around, detect_objects_360, zoom_in_object, review_image and analyze_status (three-phase evidence arbitration).
Step accounting: normalized equivalent agent steps count VLM invocations plus an extra charge per additional 3 m of NFM rollout, so the comparison with frontier-teleport baselines is fair.

setting.backbone: Frontier VLM agent (main results; named by a macro, with Qwen3.6-Plus reported at 76.7 on HM-EQA) plus a frozen Qwen-RobotNav-8B executor; ablations use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B as agent
setting.model_size: NFM 8B (also 4B ablation); agent Qwen3.5-397B-A17B for ablations
setting.training_data: none (no training; pretrained frozen foundation models composed via scaffold)
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB in four directions (front/right/back/left), pose, online explored map; no depth for the executor
setting.action_space: Semantic navigation calls to the NFM, which outputs short-horizon waypoints (8 planar waypoints) executed as navmesh-aware waypoint actions
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim 0.3.3 on HM3D scenes; real Unitree Go2
setting.privileged: none (no GT object locations or unseen geometry; the executor uses an online map built from the explored trajectory)

numbers.method: Main system with main agent + Qwen-RobotNav-8B
numbers.backbone: main agent (macro name; Qwen3.6-Plus in ablation table) + Qwen-RobotNav-8B

numbers.method: Full system with Qwen3.5-397B-A17B agent + Qwen-RobotNav-8B
numbers.evidence: Table 3 Matched full-system comparison on HM-EQA: 74.0 ± 0.3

numbers.eval_set_note: 60 real-robot episodes per method (20 per tier)
numbers.extra: real Unitree Go2; success judged manually

numbers_note: HM-EQA has 500 questions; the paper gives no split name. The episodic-interface and terminal-only accuracies are unrendered LaTeX macros (termAcc, termDelta, obsTermAcc), so they are not extractable.
results: The system reaches 76.7% on HM-EQA (+7.5 over FAST-EQA 69.2), 54.4% on MT-HM3D (+3.9 over FAST-EQA 50.5), and LLM Score 79.27 / E_path 33.96 on EXPRESS-Bench (+10.57 / +4.71). It also uses the fewest normalized agent steps. Under matched Qwen3.5 conditions it scores 74.0 vs FAST-EQA 63.5 (reproduced). On a Go2 it reaches 78.3% vs 48.3% for frontier exploration and 38.3% for the reactive baseline, with the margin growing from 10 to 45 points as the horizon grows.
limitations: Relies on a large VLM agent, which makes inference slow.
Counting is the weakest category (65.0%) because overlapping keyframes cause the same object to be counted twice.

Cross-paper comparisons are only contextual, with baselines quoted or reproduced under different conditions. Results come from a hosted API with run-to-run stochasticity, and the real-robot study is small (60 episodes per method) and lacks full ablations.
